title: Rapid recovery gating misfire causing tenant scaling lulls
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Summary: A latent race condition in the autoscaler's rapid-recovery gating logic prevented proactive scale-ups for a 7-minute window during a regional traffic spike. This manifested as repeated small lulls for several mid-market tenants that rely on reserved-burst capacity, causing increased tail latency and a handful of customer escalations. The binary symptom was: headroom estimator returned transient zero values during leader re-election, and the gating code treated this as an unrecoverable state and suppressed scale signals until a full signal epoch completed. Impact: multiple Dedicated tenants observed 4-10s cold starts and queued requests; two customers reported degraded user-facing latency and opened escalations. Root cause: gating boolean flip combined with windowed hysteresis and a short-circuit in the refill-path. During a controller restart, the estimator published partial telemetry (zeros) which was interpreted as sustained low demand; the gating code then inhibited burst replenishment. Fix: patch removes the short-circuit and adds a robust transient-value guard and leader-change backoff factor. Post-deploy monitoring shows normalized headroom and no further lulls. This ticket tracks the fix, verification, customer comms, and runbook updates.
runbook_updates: Add 'rapid-recovery gating' check to dedicated-autoscaler runbook
Document transient-zero headroom guard and leader-election backoff steps
Add checklist item for post-rolling-update headroom smoke tests
roll_forward_patch: PR 1289: remove short-circuit in gating path and add transient guard
PR 1293: conservative canary rollout config and extra telemetry tags
comments: 2026-03-05 - Alyssa Chen: Initial report from SRE after customer Slack escalation. Observed 7-minute window of repeated small lulls in us-west-2 for dedicated pools. Created ticket and triaged as P0.

2026-03-05 - Marco Rivera: Dug into allocator and controller logs. Noted leader-election events at 03:18:22 and a sequence of headroom samples that read 0 for ~90s. Suspicious gating behaviour in rapid_recovery.go:line 214.
2026-03-06 - Priya Shah (SRE): Reproduced locally by simulating controller restart under bursty traffic. Confirmed scale signals suppressed until epoch boundary.

2026-03-07 - Marco Rivera: Identified race - gating short-circuits when headroom_samples contain any zero sample and last_leader_change < epoch_window. Patch proposed to treat zeros as 'transient' unless sustained for >= 3 epochs.

2026-03-09 - Design Review: Architect team reviewed patch; agreed that treating zeros as transient is safe if we add guard rails and telemetry markers. Added extra metrics 'gating_suppressed_reason' and 'leader_change_age_ms' for debugging.
2026-03-10 - QA: Created canary profile with conservative burst thresholds. Ran workload replay against canary cluster for 6 hours. No lulls observed. Latency distributions returned to baseline.
2026-03-11 - Marco Rivera: Deployed PR 1289 to canary (10% of us-west-2 capacity) and PR 1293 to control rollout. Monitored for 24h. Observed stable headroom signals and a drop in escalations.
2026-03-12 - Customer Success: Sent interim status to affected customers summarizing root cause and mitigation steps. Offered postmortem and SLA credit where impact exceeded threshold.

2026-03-14 - Alyssa Chen: Preparing postmortem doc and runbook edits. Marking this ticket In Review for release notes and follow-ups. Next: full deployment, long-tail telemetry watch (72h), and add automated smoke test to CI that simulates leader flaps under load.
